Fixes dense renders drifting to one side, makes `--volume` set the file's level, and adds a filter for the low rumble of very dense mixes.

## Before you upgrade

- **`--volume` below 100 now makes a quieter file.** It used to apply before the limiter, so on dense music `--volume 50` mostly eased the compression while the file still peaked at full scale. Now it applies after, and 50 is half as loud all the way through. If you used it to soften the limiting, lower it less, or leave it at 100.

## What's new

- **`--dc-blocker`.** Filters out everything below 15 Hz before the limiter. Very dense mixes build up an inaudible rumble that the limiter wastes its headroom on; with this on, the music gets that headroom back and pumps less. Off by default.
- **Changing `--volume` no longer reloads the soundfont** in the guided renderer or through the API.

## Fixes

- **The densest passages no longer go hard left.** With a stereo soundfont, a block with more notes than Kestrel can hold at once kept only the left half of each note, so the right channel dropped out, sometimes for seconds. It happened in normal and per-track renders, and it happens no more.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `kestrel-1.2.1-windows-x64.zip` | Windows 10/11 |
| `kestrel-1.2.1-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS 11 or newer (Apple silicon and Intel) |
| `kestrel-1.2.1-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) |

- **Windows:** unzip and double-click `kestrel.exe`. If SmartScreen warns you, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** copy `kestrel` out of the dmg. The first time you open it, allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
- **Linux:** extract it and run `./kestrel` in a terminal. You need a Vulkan driver.

The macOS build hasn't been tested yet. If you try it, please [open an issue](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/issues) and tell us how it went.
